AccentCue.description: A one-shot SFX placed at an offset WITHIN a shot's local timeline.

at_seconds.description: Offset from the shot start, seconds
at_seconds.title: At Seconds

gain_db.description: Level trim (dB) applied to this cue
gain_db.title: Gain Db

AccentCue.title: AccentCue

AmbientCue.description:
A continuous ambient bed segment on the GLOBAL video timeline.

``end_seconds=None`` runs the bed to the end of the video. Multiple cues
let different sections carry different ambience; today the orchestrator
emits a single full-span cue, but the list shape leaves room to grow
without a schema change.

The four ``duck_*``/``sidechain_hpf_hz`` knobs below shape the sidechain
duck the SUMMED ambient bus gets under narration. They mirror ``MusicBed``'s
breathing-duck defaults and bounds EXACTLY (identical names so the renderer
reads music and ambient uniformly) because the old ambient-only duck was a
DEAD filter: it hardcoded ``threshold=0.125:release=1000``, where 0.125 is an
absolute linear key level a -18 LUFS narration bus never crosses (so the
compressor barely opened) and a 1000 ms release pinned the bed flat through
every VO gap — an ambient bed never breathed. These defaults give it the
same fast, HPF'd-key, short-release breathing shape ``MusicBed`` ships. No
``duck_db``/ratio knob: the ambient duck runs at a fixed ratio (mirroring
``MusicBed``'s effective ratio for its default ``duck_db=-12``), keeping the
surface tight. Presence-is-opt-in: a caller sending none of these still gets
the shipped breathing default.

ambient_offset_lu.description: How many LU BELOW the measured narration this ambient cue should sit. When set, the compiler MEASURES the VO bus and this asset and computes the gain; ``gain_db`` is then the fallback used only if measurement fails.
ambient_offset_lu.title: Ambient Offset Lu

duck_attack_ms.description: Sidechain attack, ms — how fast the bed dips when narration starts
duck_attack_ms.title: Duck Attack Ms

duck_open_lu_below_vo.description: When set, the sidechain open threshold is derived from the MEASURED VO level instead of the absolute ``duck_threshold``.
duck_open_lu_below_vo.title: Duck Open Lu Below Vo

duck_release_ms.description: Sidechain release, ms — how fast the bed swells back once narration stops. 700 ms is long enough that inter-WORD gaps do NOT recover (which is what made a shorter release pump once per syllable) and short enough that a real inter-SENTENCE pause still breathes
duck_release_ms.title: Duck Release Ms

duck_threshold.description: Sidechain open threshold as an ABSOLUTE linear key level (0.03 ~= -30 dBFS), fed straight to ffmpeg sidechaincompress. Ordinary narration must cross it or the compressor never opens and the bed never ducks
duck_threshold.title: Duck Threshold

end_seconds.description: End offset, seconds; None = run to end of video
end_seconds.title: End Seconds

sidechain_hpf_hz.description: High-pass applied to the sidechain KEY (not the audible narration) so the duck triggers on speech presence rather than rumble / plosives / room tone
sidechain_hpf_hz.title: Sidechain Hpf Hz

AmbientCue.title: AmbientCue

Callout.description:
One per-shot callout bound to a clicked element (ORCH-3.2 directed footage).

A ``badge`` draws a tinted numbered disc glued to the element's top-left
corner (its ``label`` is the short number/text centered on the disc); a
``label`` draws a short caption anchored to the element bbox; a ``spotlight``
dims the bbox-complement to isolate the element; an ``arrow`` overlays a small
triangle sprite pointing at the element. ``bbox`` is ``(x, y, w, h)`` in
RECORDED source pixels — the SAME convention as ``FocusKey.bbox`` — so the
renderer remaps it through the same fit transform before compositing. Callouts
ride the PRE-zoom canvas so a focus punch-in magnifies them with the element.

bbox.description: Clicked-element region (x, y, w, h) in RECORDED source pixels (same convention as FocusKey.bbox)
bbox.title: Bbox

label.description: L3 callout copy; badge → short number/text
label.title: Label

Callout.title: Callout

CaptionCue.description:
One word- or phrase-timed caption, in the SHOT's local timeline (seconds).

``start``/``end`` are shot-local; the renderer maps them onto the film bus
(applying the shot's ``speed`` retime and clamping to the shot's on-screen
window) when it builds the burned-in ASS subtitle track. ``end`` must be
strictly greater than ``start``.

``words`` — the cue's per-word timings — is optional; it powers karaoke
``{\k}`` word-highlight when a compile sets ``captions_karaoke`` and renders
``burned_in``. ``None``/absent ⇒ the whole cue highlights as one phrase.

words.description: Optional per-word timings (shot-local) for karaoke highlight. Used only when the compile sets `captions_karaoke` in `burned_in` mode; None (default) ⇒ the cue highlights as a single phrase.
words.title: Words

CaptionCue.title: CaptionCue

CaptionWord.description:
One word's shot-local ``[start, end)`` timing, for karaoke ``{\k}`` highlight.

Shot-local seconds, mapped onto the film bus with the SAME offset/÷speed/clamp
math as the parent cue. Only consumed when a compile requests
``captions_karaoke`` in ``burned_in`` mode; otherwise ignored.
CaptionWord.title: CaptionWord

ColorAdjust.description:
Per-shot colour grade applied as an ffmpeg ``eq`` pass.

Every numeric knob defaults to its identity value (a grade that changes
nothing), so an all-default ``ColorAdjust`` with no ``preset`` emits no
filter at all and the render stays byte-identical to before this field
existed. ``preset`` expands to a fixed grade (warm/cool/bw/vivid/cinematic);
any explicitly-set numeric field overrides the matching preset component.

preset.description: Named grade expanded to a fixed eq; explicitly-set numeric fields override the matching preset component. None = no preset.
preset.title: Preset

ColorAdjust.title: ColorAdjust

CursorKey.description:
One keyframe of a synthetic cursor path (ORCH-3.2 directed footage).

``t`` is the shot-local second; ``x``/``y`` are the cursor tip position in
the RENDER frame's pixel space (the same frame-pixel space the VP-2 capture
producer emits — CSS px x capture_scale). ``click`` marks a click at this
keyframe, which triggers a brief expanding click-pulse ring. Between
keyframes the renderer smoothstep-eases the position. An absent
``cursor_track`` (the default) synthesises no cursor and is byte-identical.

click.description: A click fires here → click-pulse ring
click.title: Click

t.description: Shot-local time of this keyframe, seconds
t.title: T

CursorKey.title: CursorKey

FinishProfile.description:
Per-job finishing/delivery overrides (VC-5): the brand letterbox colour.

Presence-is-opt-in, exactly like ``MasteringProfile``: an absent ``finish``
(or an all-default one) changes no filter string, so the render stays
byte-identical to before this field existed. The colour folds onto the
per-shot filter chain — the final concat is a stream copy, so there is no
whole-film finishing pass to hang it on.

A ``broadcast_safe`` legal-luma flag was designed here and CUT: a pre-encode
clamp cannot guarantee a decoded 16..235 master (libx264 ringing around text
re-introduces illegal values, worsening with CRF) and the flag would have
been a lie. See the note in ``renderer`` above ``_pad_color``.

grade.description: Whole-film colour grade (VC-5): a single post-concat re-encode over the delivered timeline. None — or a disabled/all-identity grade — is a no-op, byte-identical to before this field existed.

letterbox_color.description: Brand letterbox/pillarbox fill as #RRGGBB (or #RRGGBBAA), e.g. '#101820'. None (default) keeps the service's render_bg_color. The hex pattern is also the injection guard — this value is interpolated into the ffmpeg filtergraph's pad `color=` option.
letterbox_color.title: Letterbox Color

FinishProfile.title: FinishProfile

FocusKey.description:
One keyframe of a focus/auto-zoom track (ORCH-3.2 directed footage).

``bbox`` is ``(x, y, w, h)`` in RENDER-frame pixel space — the region the
punch-in should frame (a clicked control, a highlighted panel). The renderer
eases a ``zoompan`` punch-in centered on the bbox and back out. An absent
``focus_track`` (the default) applies no zoom and is byte-identical.

bbox.description: Focus region (x, y, w, h) in render-frame pixels
bbox.title: Bbox

t.description: Shot-local time of this keyframe, seconds
t.title: T

FocusKey.title: FocusKey

GradeSpec.description:
Whole-film colour grade applied as ONE post-concat re-encode pass (VC-5).

Unlike the per-shot ``ColorAdjust`` (which folds an ``eq`` onto each segment
before the stream-copy concat), this grades the ENTIRE finished timeline in a
single pass over the delivery master — a film-wide "look" with split-toning,
vignette, grain, sharpen, glow and an optional broadcast-legal clamp.

Presence-is-opt-in and identity-is-no-op: ``enabled=False`` (the default), or
an ``enabled`` grade whose every knob sits at its identity default, emits an
EMPTY filter chain (``renderer._grade_vf`` → ``""``), so the compile keeps the
``-c copy`` fast path and stays byte-identical to a pre-VC-5 render. Only a
grade that actually moves a knob triggers the whole-film re-encode.

Field names + clamps mirror the orchestrator's ``finish.GradeSpec`` byte-for-
byte so a request round-trips unchanged. Tints are accepted permissively (3-
or 6-digit hex, leading ``#`` optional) — a stricter pattern here would 422 a
valid orchestrator payload; an unparseable tint degrades to a neutral (no-op)
split-tone rather than rejecting the compile.

broadcast_safe.description: Append a best-effort legal-range (16..235) luma clamp as the LAST filter — the colour analog of the true-peak limiter, not a hard guarantee (x264 ringing can re-introduce a few illegal codes).
broadcast_safe.title: Broadcast Safe

enabled.description: Master opt-in; False (default) emits no grade (byte-identical)
enabled.title: Enabled

grade_intensity.description: Global dry/wet on the whole grade (1 = full, 0 = identity/no-op)
grade_intensity.title: Grade Intensity

highlight_tint.description: Split-tone colour pushed into the highlights; #ffffff (default) = no tint
highlight_tint.title: Highlight Tint

look.description: Named base look expanded to a fixed eq (warm/cool/bw/vivid/cinematic reuse the per-shot presets); a free string — an unknown look is a no-op base, not a 422. 'none' (default) adds no base grade.
look.title: Look

lut_url.description: Optional 3D-LUT reference. Carried on the contract + report for forward-compat; LUT application is not performed by this service.
lut_url.title: Lut Url

match_sources.description: Bias the grade's luma/saturation midpoints toward the delivered film's own measured signalstats (best-effort; a measurement miss silently falls back to the un-biased grade).
match_sources.title: Match Sources

shadow_tint.description: Split-tone colour pushed into the shadows; #000000 (default) = no shadow tint
shadow_tint.title: Shadow Tint

temperature.description: Warm/cool bias (-1 cool .. +1 warm; 0 = neutral), applied as a per-channel gamma
temperature.title: Temperature

GradeSpec.title: GradeSpec

MasteringProfile.description:
Per-job overrides for the encode/delivery master (VC-2, contract C11).

Every field is optional; an omitted/out-of-range value degrades to the
service default (never a 5xx) via the same clamp discipline as the compile
``tags``. These fold into the tag-resolution path in the compile route, so
the picture master can be retargeted per run without a redeploy.

bitrate_mode.description: Rate control: auto (CRF only) / vbv / cbr / capped
bitrate_mode.title: Bitrate Mode

maxrate.description: VBV peak bitrate (e.g. '12M'); only used under a VBV mode
maxrate.title: Maxrate

MasteringProfile.title: MasteringProfile

MusicBed.description:
Continuous music under the whole video, ducked beneath narration.

Request-level (not per-shot) because it spans the entire timeline — a
per-shot music input would restart at every cut. Looped to fill the video,
faded in/out, and sidechain-ducked under the concatenated narration.

The duck is a ``sidechaincompress`` keyed off the narration bus. ``duck_db``
sets its DEPTH (mapped to the compression ratio); the four knobs below set
its TIMING and SENSITIVITY. Their defaults are the shipped behaviour — a
caller that sends none of them still gets a duck that opens on ordinary
narration and breathes back in the gaps.

duck_attack_ms.description: Sidechain attack, ms — how fast the bed dips when narration starts
duck_attack_ms.title: Duck Attack Ms

duck_db.description: Advisory extra attenuation under narration; tunes the sidechain compressor
duck_db.title: Duck Db

duck_open_lu_below_vo.description: When set, the sidechain open threshold is derived from the MEASURED VO level instead of the absolute ``duck_threshold``.
duck_open_lu_below_vo.title: Duck Open Lu Below Vo

duck_release_ms.description: Sidechain release, ms — how fast the bed swells back once narration stops. 700 ms is long enough that inter-WORD gaps do NOT recover (which is what made a shorter release pump once per syllable) and short enough that a real inter-SENTENCE pause still breathes
duck_release_ms.title: Duck Release Ms

duck_threshold.description: Sidechain open threshold as an ABSOLUTE linear key level (0.03 ~= -30 dBFS), fed straight to ffmpeg sidechaincompress. Ordinary narration must cross it or the compressor never opens and the bed never ducks. A measured / VO-relative threshold is a documented follow-up, not this knob
duck_threshold.title: Duck Threshold

music_offset_lu.description: How many LU BELOW the measured narration the bed should sit. When set, the compiler MEASURES the VO bus and the music asset and computes the gain; ``gain_db`` is then the fallback used only if measurement fails.
music_offset_lu.title: Music Offset Lu

sidechain_hpf_hz.description: High-pass applied to the sidechain KEY (not the audible narration) so the duck triggers on speech presence rather than rumble / plosives / room tone
sidechain_hpf_hz.title: Sidechain Hpf Hz

MusicBed.title: MusicBed

OverlayClip.description:
An animated graphic with a REAL ALPHA CHANNEL composited ON TOP of the shot.

This is the true overlay layer — a lower-third that flies in over drone
footage, a persistent logo bug — as opposed to a full-frame animated card,
which needs nothing new (it is an ordinary ``Shot`` with a ``video_url``).

``url`` is the same reference shape as every other asset (presigned MinIO
http(s), ``file://``, or a bare local path) and is fetched through the same
per-job dedupe, so one logo bug reused on twenty shots downloads once. An
unfetchable overlay DROPS that overlay and logs; it never fails the compile.

THE PRODUCER SHIPS VP9 WEBM WITH ALPHA. Alpha does not ride in the pixel
format — a correct file reports ``pix_fmt=yuv420p`` and carries the WebM
container tag ``alpha_mode=1``, with the alpha plane in ``BlockAdditional``
side data. Anything that "validates alpha" by looking for ``yuva420p`` will
reject every correct build. See ``renderer._inject_overlay_clips`` for the
decoder trap this costs on the ffmpeg side.

Times are SHOT-LOCAL seconds on the shot's own (pre-``speed``) timeline —
see ``retime_with_speed``.

duration_seconds.description: How long the overlay stays on screen, seconds. None (default) = the overlay's own natural length, after which it disappears (it does NOT freeze on its last frame).
duration_seconds.title: Duration Seconds

opacity.description: Uniform multiplier on the graphic's OWN alpha (1.0 = default, the authored alpha untouched and byte-identical; 0 = fully transparent).
opacity.title: Opacity

retime_with_speed.description: Whether ``start_seconds``/``duration_seconds`` are read on the shot's SOURCE timeline (True, default) or on the RENDERED one (False). The overlay is a separate ffmpeg input and is NOT touched by the shot's ``speed`` retime, so True divides both times by ``speed`` — a cue authored against the source stays glued to the frame it was authored for. False pins the overlay to wall-clock output time instead (a logo bug that must appear 2s into the delivered segment regardless of how the picture was retimed). At ``speed=1.0`` the two are identical.
retime_with_speed.title: Retime With Speed

scale.description: 'fit' (default) scales the graphic to fit INSIDE the render canvas preserving its aspect (no crop, no pad — the alpha carries the framing), so one 1920x1080 authored asset lands correctly at every output tier. 'native' composites it at its authored pixel size.
scale.title: Scale

start_seconds.description: Shot-local onset, seconds; 0 (default) = visible from the shot's first frame
start_seconds.title: Start Seconds

x.description: ffmpeg overlay x expression in CANVAS pixels — a bare number, or an expression over W/H (canvas) and w/h (overlay), e.g. '(W-w)/2' to centre or 'W-w-64' to pin right. Charset-constrained (no ':' ',' or quotes) because it is interpolated into the filtergraph.
x.title: X

y.description: ffmpeg overlay y expression in canvas pixels; same charset rules as ``x``
y.title: Y

OverlayClip.title: OverlayClip

adjust.description: Optional per-shot colour grade (ffmpeg eq), applied after scale/pad. None — or an all-default grade with no preset — is a no-op, byte-identical to before this field existed.

audio.description: Per-shot primary-audio gain/mute/fade. None is a no-op — byte-identical.

audio_url.description: Narration audio muxed over this shot; sets the shot duration
audio_url.title: Audio Url

callouts.description: Optional per-shot callouts (badge/label/spotlight/arrow) bound to the clicked element bbox in recorded px; None/[] ⇒ no-op, byte-identical. The renderer composites at most the first few (see _CALLOUT_MAX_PER_SHOT).
callouts.title: Callouts

clip_anchor.description: Where within a footage clip the shown window sits. 'start' (default) plays from the beginning (optionally after ``clip_lead_seconds``). 'end' shows the clip's SETTLED TAIL — the last ``duration`` seconds — so a slow app load / zoom-in at the head is skipped and only the final hero state (a fitted floor plan, a loaded page) appears. Zero leading load-in / white frames. Ignored for image/text shots.
clip_anchor.title: Clip Anchor

clip_lead_seconds.description: For ``clip_anchor='start'``: seconds to skip at the head of the footage clip (trim the app's white load-in) before the shown window. Bounded so the remaining clip still covers the shot duration.
clip_lead_seconds.title: Clip Lead Seconds

clip_out_seconds.description: Source-timeline OUT-point, in seconds from the head of the footage clip. Together with ``clip_lead_seconds`` (the in-point) it names an explicit window: ``clip_lead_seconds=4.0, clip_out_seconds=7.5`` shows exactly 4.0s to 7.5s of the source. That is the only way to cut SEVERAL shots out of ONE long recording; without it the out-point is merely implied by ``seconds`` and every shot replays from the same in-point. Measured on the SOURCE timeline, so it is independent of ``speed`` (a 3.5s window at speed=2.0 renders as a 1.75s segment). Clamped to the real clip length; a window shorter than the shot's narration freeze-pads as usual. Must be greater than ``clip_lead_seconds``. Ignored for image/text shots. None (default) is a no-op, byte-identical to before this field existed.
clip_out_seconds.title: Clip Out Seconds

cursor_track.description: Synthetic cursor path (ORCH-3.2): a brand-tinted disc overlaid on the shot, smoothstep-eased between keyframes, with a click-pulse ring on click keyframes. None (default) synthesises no cursor — byte-identical.
cursor_track.title: Cursor Track

description.description: Text drawn on a solid card when no image_url/video_url is given
description.title: Description

fit.description: How the visual fills the frame. 'contain' (default) fits-inside + pads (letter/pillarbox) so nothing is cropped — for footage/slides/screenshots. 'cover' scales-to-fill + center-crops so the frame is full — for atmospheric AI-image backgrounds, killing the navy bars. 'scroll' fits a tall full-page screenshot to the frame width and pans it top→bottom over the shot — for website-review captures that would otherwise letterbox to an unreadable vertical sliver.
fit.title: Fit

focus_track.description: Auto-zoom track (ORCH-3.2): a punch-in eased onto the focus bbox and back out (ffmpeg zoompan), applied after fit/scale and before the look. None (default) applies no zoom — byte-identical to before this field.
focus_track.title: Focus Track

footage_viewport.description: (width, height) in pixels of the recorded source video the focus_track/cursor_track coordinates were captured in. When set and != the render canvas, the renderer remaps those coords through the same decrease-scale+centered-pad transform used to fit the source, so cursor/zoom land on-target at any output tier. None => coords assumed already in render-canvas pixels (legacy/identity).
footage_viewport.title: Footage Viewport

image_url.description: Still frame held for the shot duration (slide PNG / screenshot / AI image)
image_url.title: Image Url

max_seconds.description: Upper bound (clip length + freeze-pad ceiling) the orchestrator's reconcile_timeline stamped for a footage beat carrying over-length narration. Advisory unless the ``freeze_pad_cap`` render tag is on: when set, the freeze-pad DRIFT is bounded to end at ``max_seconds`` instead of ramping over the whole narration, so an over-narrated footage clip stops drifting at the ceiling and settles for the tail (the video still fills the full audio — no black, no truncated audio). None (default) or the tag off is a no-op — byte-identical to before this field existed.
max_seconds.title: Max Seconds

overlay_clips.description: Animated graphics with a real alpha channel composited ON TOP of this shot's picture (lower-thirds, logo bugs), after the grade/titles. At most 2 per shot. Empty (default) is a no-op — no extra ffmpeg input, no extra filter, byte-identical to before this field existed. A FULL-FRAME animated card is not this: it is an ordinary shot with a ``video_url``.
overlay_clips.title: Overlay Clips

overlays.description: Burned-in text titles (drawtext) drawn on this shot after the grade. Empty (default) is a no-op.
overlays.title: Overlays

retime.description: Optional per-shot retiming hint onto the master cadence: 'clean' (frame drop/dup), 'motion' (motion-compensated interpolation), or 'budget' (cheap blend). Only bites when this shot's ``target_fps`` is a NON-integer ratio of the master cadence — an exact ratio is always the clean drop/dup. Advisory; unset/unknown falls back to the service-wide ``render_motion_blur`` (off by default = clean).
retime.title: Retime

seconds.description: Requested wall-clock duration. For a silent visual-only shot this IS the length. When ``audio_url`` is set AND ``max_seconds`` is set (a shot the orchestrator's reconcile_timeline bounded) it is a FLOOR: the segment lasts ``max(probed narration, seconds)``, so the narration is never cut and a plan that pins a footage beat to its measured clip (the orchestrator clamps ``seconds`` into reconcile_timeline's ``[min, max]`` window) is honoured instead of being shortened to the narration; the audio after the narration is silence. Without ``max_seconds`` a narrated shot's ``seconds`` may be a storyboard guess and is ignored (narration length). A floor within one output frame of the narration is ignored. A clip that carries its OWN audio (no ``audio_url``) still plays at its natural length. Bounded so one shot can't request a multi-year render.
seconds.title: Seconds

sfx.description: Accent SFX mixed in at offsets within the shot
sfx.title: Sfx

speed.description: Per-clip playback speed factor. Retimes BOTH this shot's video (setpts) and its audio (atempo) so the rendered segment lasts 1/speed of its source: 2.0 = twice as fast / half the length, 0.5 = half speed. 1.0 (default) is a no-op — byte-identical to before this field existed.
speed.title: Speed

split.description: Composite two sources into the shot canvas via hstack/vstack (ORCH-3.2 T8). None (default) is a no-op — byte-identical to before this field existed. On a split shot the renderer disables cursor/callout/zoom/speed (their coords are in the primary's full-canvas px).

target_fps.description: Declared source frame rate of this shot's visual (VC-3). Feeds the master-cadence selector so the whole compile snaps onto one retime-cost-minimal output rate. Advisory — an omitted value simply doesn't bias the selection; the render still snaps to the master rate.
target_fps.title: Target Fps

transition.description: Crossfade INTO this shot from the previous one (xfade/acrossfade). Ignored on the first shot. Setting it on ANY shot switches the whole compile from the fast stream-copy concat to a re-encoding xfade join.

transition_sfx.description: One-shot SFX mixed in at this shot's cut-in (t=0)

video_url.description: Pre-recorded clip (keeps its own audio unless audio_url overrides)
video_url.title: Video Url

ShotCaptions.description:
The caption cues for one shot, addressed by its index in the shot list.

``shot_index`` is the 0-based position of the shot in ``CompileRequest.shots``.
An empty ``cues`` list contributes nothing to the burned-in track.
ShotCaptions.title: ShotCaptions

SoundCue.description:
A one-shot SFX played at the start of a shot (transition whoosh/pop).

``url`` is the same reference shape as ``audio_url`` (presigned MinIO
http(s), ``file://``, or a bare local path). ``gain_db`` is a level trim
fed straight to ffmpeg ``volume=<gain_db>dB`` (0 = unchanged).

gain_db.description: Level trim (dB) applied to this cue
gain_db.title: Gain Db

SoundCue.title: SoundCue

second_source_url.description: Resolved URL of the SECOND video composited beside the primary. The primary source drives the shot duration; both halves are letterboxed into their half-canvas.
second_source_url.title: Second Source Url

TextOverlay.description:
A burned-in text title drawn on a shot via ffmpeg ``drawtext``.

``position`` anchors the text at one of nine safe-area points; an explicit
``x``/``y`` (pixels from the top-left) overrides the anchor. ``start``/``end``
(shot-local seconds) gate the overlay's visibility via an ``enable=between``
expression; both unset shows it for the whole shot.

end.description: Hide after this shot-local second (None = to the end)
end.title: End

position.description: Nine-grid anchor; overridden by explicit x/y
position.title: Position

start.description: Show from this shot-local second (None = from the start)
start.title: Start

x.description: Explicit x (px from left); overrides position
x.title: X

y.description: Explicit y (px from top); overrides position
y.title: Y

TextOverlay.title: TextOverlay

Transition.description:
A visual crossfade INTO a shot from the PREVIOUS one.

A shot's ``transition`` describes how the cut ENTERING that shot behaves, so
the first shot's ``transition`` is meaningless (no preceding shot to dissolve
from) and is ignored. ``type`` selects an ffmpeg ``xfade`` transition;
``dissolve`` is an alias for the plain ``fade`` cross-dissolve. ``duration``
is the overlap length in seconds; at render time it is clamped to the shorter
of the two adjacent segments so a crossfade can never exceed either clip.

When ANY shot in a compile carries a ``transition`` the compiler leaves the
fast stream-copy concat path and joins segments through a re-encoding
``xfade``/``acrossfade`` chain instead; a compile with no transitions is
byte-identical to before this field existed.

duration.description: Crossfade overlap, seconds; clamped to the shorter adjacent clip
duration.title: Duration

Transition.title: Transition

ambient.description: Continuous ambient bed segments on the global timeline
ambient.title: Ambient

cadence.description: Per-job master-cadence override (VC-3). When set, the whole compile renders at this rate (snapped to the nearest legal cadence {24,25,30,50,60}), bypassing the auto retime-cost selector. Omitted → auto selection from the shots' declared source rates / render_fps.
cadence.title: Cadence

caption_box_colour.description: Burned-in caption box colour as '#RRGGBB' (e.g. '#0B1F3A'). When this or `caption_box_opacity` is set, each cue is drawn on ONE continuous box (libass BorderStyle=4) instead of the default per-line plate; the unset one falls back to black / the default plate opacity. None (default) ⇒ unchanged. Ignored in 'overlay' mode.
caption_box_colour.title: Caption Box Colour

caption_box_opacity.description: Opacity of the caption box, 0 (clear) .. 1 (solid). See `caption_box_colour`. None (default) ⇒ unchanged.
caption_box_opacity.title: Caption Box Opacity

caption_font_family.description: Font family for burned-in captions, from the fonts this service embeds: 'Inter' (Inter 4.1, OFL — SemiBold 600, Bold 700 when the caption mood is bold; matches the film cards) or 'DejaVu Sans' (the default). None (default) ⇒ the default font, byte-identical. Ignored in 'overlay' mode.
caption_font_family.title: Caption Font Family

caption_mood.description: Run-level mood token (e.g. 'energetic', 'calm', 'confident') that selects a per-video caption look (colour/outline/size/weight), so the caption styling tracks the same mood that drives the colour grade. None (default) or an unrecognised value ⇒ the default `Cap` style, byte-identical to before this field existed.
caption_mood.title: Caption Mood

caption_text_colour.description: Burned-in caption text colour as '#RRGGBB' (e.g. '#F8FAFC'). Overrides the mood's text colour. None (default) ⇒ unchanged. Ignored in 'overlay' mode.
caption_text_colour.title: Caption Text Colour

captions.description: Word/phrase-timed burned-in captions (VC-6), one entry per shot carrying cues. Cues are mapped onto the film bus and rendered as a single libass ASS subtitle pass folded into the SAME whole-film grade re-encode. None (default) — or no emitted cues — is a no-op, byte-identical to before this field existed.
captions.title: Captions

captions_karaoke.description: When True AND `captions_render` is 'burned_in', render each cue's per-word `words` as ASS {\k} karaoke highlight; a cue with no words highlights as one phrase. No effect in 'overlay' mode (soft subtitle tracks cannot carry {\k}) or when `captions` is None. False (default) ⇒ plain phrase captions, byte-identical.
captions_karaoke.title: Captions Karaoke

captions_render.description: How the word-timed captions in `captions` are rendered. 'overlay' (default) muxes them as a selectable soft mov_text subtitle track (players toggle on/off) — no burn, no video re-encode. 'burned_in' bakes them into the picture in the whole-film re-encode and must be requested explicitly: subtitles are never burned in by default. Ignored when `captions` is None.
captions_render.title: Captions Render

emit_shot_timeline.description: When true, the response carries a per-shot `shot_timeline` (authoritative `[start,end)` per beat on the final mux). Off by default so the plain concat fast path stays probe-free.
emit_shot_timeline.title: Emit Shot Timeline

finish.description: Per-job finishing overrides (VC-5): the brand letterbox/pillarbox colour, applied on the per-shot filter chain. None (default) is a no-op — byte-identical to before this field existed.

master_lufs.description: Per-job override for the loudness-master integrated-loudness target (LUFS). Folded into ``tags['master_lufs']`` and clamped to [-30, -5] via the same path as the tag; out-of-range values are ignored.
master_lufs.title: Master Lufs

mastering.description: Per-job encode/delivery master overrides (colorspace, deband, bitrate mode, CRF, loudness target, platform). Folded into the tag-resolution clamp path; out-of-range values degrade to defaults.

music.description: Continuous music bed under the whole video, ducked under narration
